clearedSpotChecks.check: A sync of a native face made before an unlock on Celo, Arc and Polygon, where an ERC-20 address measures the native balance: can one payment be credited under address(0) and under the face, and what does a native payout do while the face is synced.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read the lines first. A value credit needs the currency slot to be zero (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). A balance credit needs a nonzero slot, rejects value (356) and resets the slot (361), and every sync reads the balance again (285-286). settle and settleFor are the only payable functions (300, 305) and src/ outside src/test has no receive or fallback function, so no other call can bring value in. One inflow is therefore credited under one id. test/Sync.t.sol:255-277 expects the same revert for a contract that reports native balances. I then ran my own sequence with my own driver, one eth_call per network with state overrides on 2026-11-23: Celo block 83,545,609 (https://forno.celo.org), Arc block 32,753,089 (https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io), Polygon block 97,827,270 (https://polygon.drpc.org). With the face synced before the unlock, settleFor and settle with 777 wei both reverted with NonzeroNativeValue. A native take followed by a zero value settle reverted with a Panic. After sync(address(0)) a value settle repaid the take. A payment through the face (300 wei on Celo, 3 units on Arc) was credited once under the face id, a second sync and settle paid 0, and a settle with nothing synced and no value paid 0. A claim minted under the face id could not be burned under id 0 (Panic). A native take against the face credit left two open deltas, and only a take under the face id plus a native repayment closed them. At the end every delta read 0 and the native balance of the PoolManager equalled its starting value on all three networks (about 6,111.59 CELO, 2,448,892.23 USDC and 3,082,288.23 POL). On Polygon the transfer through 0x1010 reverted and a take under that id reverted with WrappedError, as the item says. One addition for Arc. balanceOf at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 is the native balance divided by 10^12 and rounded down (2448892234477 units against 2448892234477765867401833 wei at that block). A native inflow of less than 10^12 wei that arrives while the face is synced and lifts the remainder over 10^12 would be credited as one whole unit. settle rejects value in that state, so this needs an inflow that bypasses settle, and the gain is below 10^12 wei (0.000001 USDC) per settle. I did not test whether Arc permits such an inflow. It is recorded as a low lead. The chain tests ran on the contracts deployed today and do not test a build of this checkout, which the open lead of core-code-test-pins on compiling the checkout covers.

clearedSpotChecks.check: A take of a currency address without code succeeds because the transfer accepts empty return data (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74), while src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:174 says take reverts if the amount is not available. What can an ordinary account do with that, and can a pool, a claim or a debt exist under such an address.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code. The token branch of transfer accepts a call that does not revert and returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74), and take books the debit before the call (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295), so a take of a codeless currency leaves its caller with a debt and moves nothing. balanceOfSelf is a high level call that needs 32 bytes of return data (Currency.sol:94), so sync reverts for such an address and settle cannot credit it. The other sources of a positive delta are burn, which needs a claim that mint creates only against an equal debit (322-336), pool amounts, which Pool.sol:206-237 and SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288 round against the caller, and hook deltas, which Hooks.sol:230, 242 and 312 subtract from the caller. I checked those lines. Inside one unlock the deltas in such a currency sum to zero or less, the party with the debt cannot close (112), and so no claim under that id survives an unlock. Chain. My own driver on all 21 rpc URLs of networks.json at the latest block on 2026-11-23 (Monad after one retry for a rate limit): take of 5 units of a codeless address succeeded and the delta slot read minus 5, sync of it reverted with empty data, settleFor paid 0, burn reverted with a Panic, clear reverted with MustClearExactPositiveDelta, an unlock that only took 5 reverted with CurrencyNotSettled and one that took 0 closed. The address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000100 gave the same two answers on all 21 (take succeeds, sync reverts). A stateless precompile returns the same bytes for the same input, so where sync does accept its answer the rise between sync and settle is 0. For the fork part that the next item builds on this one, I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/params/config.go (line 256 sets JennerTime to 1796697000, which is 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/evm.go (lines 46 to 58 resolve CAS20 addresses from the prefix once Jenner is active). 0xca52000000000000000001217954ab5467577565 holds no code on BNB Smart Chain at block 135,292,596 and answers balanceOf, transfer and empty calldata from the PoolManager address with success and no data. On Chapel at block 144,426,465 it holds the code 0xef, answers balanceOf with 32 bytes and reverts on transfer of 1, and the never created address 0xca52000000000000000000000000000000abcdef reverts on all three shapes. The chain tests ran on the contracts deployed today and do not test a build of this checkout, which the open lead of core-code-test-pins on compiling the checkout covers.

clearedSpotChecks.check: settle and settleFor credit msg.value when no currency is synced and read no balance (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). Does the deployed code credit exactly the value sent, does the guard at line 356 hold, and did this unit find a frame that carries value nobody paid.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code. _settle credits msg.value only when the currency slot is zero and reads no balance in that branch (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). With a nonzero slot it rejects value (356). settle and settleFor are the only payable functions (300, 305). The credit is therefore exactly the CALLVALUE of the frame, and the question is whether a frame can report a value that nobody paid. Chain. On each of the 21 rpc URLs I sent one eth_call with value 1 from an address with balance 0 to a stub that returns CALLVALUE (code by state override). It failed on all 21: OutOfFunds or insufficient funds on 20, and value transfer not allowed on Tempo, where the same call from any sender fails with that message. An ordinary sender therefore cannot state a value it does not hold on any of the networks. My face runs on Celo, Arc and Polygon returned the value sent from settle (300 wei, 3*10^12 wei and 300 wei) and my runs with a token synced reverted with NonzeroNativeValue, which matches the item. On Arc the same call from the zero address reverts with Zero address not allowed. Limits. I did not reread the transaction type walks of cycle 3 that the item relies on for the absence of other frames with unpaid value. The verifiers of arbitrum-family and op-stack-custom-gas confirmed those walks in this cycle for Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Celo and X Layer. F-058 on BNB Smart Chain remains the only recorded frame of that kind, and it needs the system address as caller. On Tempo an inner CALL with value works when the calling stub is given a balance by state override, as the item says. I did not check whether any account on Tempo holds a real native balance. A cleared item of cycle 1 for chain 4217 states that the client rejects transactions with value, and my call confirms that for the top level. The chain tests ran on the contracts deployed today and do not test a build of this checkout, which the open lead of core-code-test-pins on compiling the checkout covers.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Caller identities that a network creates, against the functions that trust msg.sender without a lock or a role: unlock, sync, the ERC-6909 functions, and the controller check, which the zero address passes on 13 networks.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Reproduced on the 21 rpc URLs on 2026-11-23: unlock from an address without code reverts with empty data, the zero address holds no code, its nonce is 10 on OP Mainnet, Zora and World Chain, 8 on Base, 7 on Unichain, Ink and Soneium, 5 on Celo, 2 on X Layer and 0 on the other twelve, and protocolFeeController reads zero on 13 networks. The check at src/PoolManager.sol:110 and the controller checks at src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48 are as cited. The item left the nonces untraced. I traced them by a search on eth_getTransactionCount at past blocks. Unichain: three transactions from the zero address in block 16,058,042, two in block 33,942,842 and two in block 52,778,042 (time 1783526401, 2026-07-08). Celo: three in block 40,172,442 and two in block 63,058,030. X Layer: two in block 45,922,165. OP Mainnet: two in block 144,546,212 and two in block 153,963,812, and I did not trace the six older ones there. Every one of them is a deposit of type 0x7e with value 0 and mint 0 that calls upgradeTo(address) (selector 0x3659cfe6) on a predeploy proxy: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000015, ...0f and ...1b, and in the July 2026 bundle ...2c and ...18. The OP Stack specifications define such deposits with the zero address as sender and fixed target and data: two in Ecotone, one in Fjord, three in Isthmus and two in Jovian (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/main/specs/protocol/ecotone/derivation.md lines 224 and 254, fjord/derivation.md line 211, isthmus/derivation.md lines 202, 232 and 262, jovian/derivation.md lines 112 and 201). The data of the Jovian L1Block update in the specification equals the data seen on Unichain, Celo, X Layer and OP Mainnet. I found no specification text for the July 2026 bundle. The sender, target and data of these deposits are fixed by the fork rules, so the actor is governance, and this answers part of the open leads L-100 and L-129. Arc. I fetched the three files the item cites. crates/evm/src/evm.rs lines 660 to 669 reject a caller of the precompile that is not on its list, lines 1666 to 1677 put only the Memo and Multicall3From addresses on that list, lines 893 to 903 reject every scheme other than CALL, and lines 946 to 955 reject a named sender that is neither the caller of the precompile nor the sender of the transaction. Memo.sol line 43 and Multicall3From.sol lines 43, 58, 81 and 161 pass msg.sender. A child call therefore carries the signing account as sender only when that account itself called the helper, and code that runs in the middle of another account's transaction is refused. Reach if the premise failed: a caller with the zero address as msg.sender could set a protocol fee of at most 0.1 percent per direction and collect what then accrues, and nothing else (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-57, checked subtraction at 55).

clearedSpotChecks.check: The reverse of the missing noDelegateCall: a contract that the PoolManager has called forwards transfer and balanceOf to an enshrined token by DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE. Does the token act with the PoolManager as holder, and what does an account whose EIP-7702 designator names such a token answer. Base and Tempo at the releases that run today (standing lead L-406), with the delegated account part also on Arc and Celo.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The item ran the forwarder test on Tempo and Base and only the delegated account part on Arc and Celo. I ran the missing part on those two networks, where the PoolManager holds about 2.45 million USDC and 6,111 CELO as native balance. Method as in the item: read-only eth_call, the measuring stub at the PoolManager address, a forwarder stub in between. Arc, blocks 32,754,079 and 32,754,137. A forwarder that sends transfer(sink, 1) to 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 by DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE gets success with no data and nothing moves, because the proxy code finds no implementation pointer in the forwarder's storage. With the pointer of the real proxy (slot 0x7050c9e0f4ca769c69bd3a8ef740bc37934f8e2c036e5a723fd8ee048ed3f8c3, value 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6) placed in the forwarder's storage, the token logic runs with the PoolManager as inherited caller and reverts with Not enabled for native coin transfers under DELEGATECALL, and with ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance under CALLCODE. Direct, DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE calls of transfer shapes to the precompiles 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000000, ...01 and ...02 all reverted. The native balance and the face balance of the PoolManager were the same before and after, and the direct transfer of 1 unit in the same call moved 10^12 wei. This matches the client source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_authority.rs lines 300 to 314 require the caller to be 0x3600... and reject a frame whose target or code address is not the precompile (helpers.rs lines 565 to 587), and line 56 holds the error text I received. Celo, block 83,546,189. With the implementation pointer of the CELO token (0xfea1b35f1d5f2a58532a70e7a32e6f2d3bc4f7b1) in the forwarder's storage, transfer(sink, 1) reverted with CELO transfer failed under DELEGATECALL and with transfer value exceeded balance of sender under CALLCODE. Calls to the transfer precompile 0xfd with (PoolManager, sink, 1) reverted when sent directly, by DELEGATECALL and by CALLCODE. Balances were unchanged, and the direct CELO transfer of 1 in the same call moved 1 wei. One fact to add to the item: such a forwarder answers balanceOf(PoolManager) with the real native balance on both networks, so any account can make one more id that mirrors the native balance. That is the class of F-050 and F-008 and of src/test/NativeERC20.sol:46-48. It gives no credit, because value cannot enter through settle while the mirror is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356) and the mirror's transfer moves nothing. The lead L-406 stays open for the next releases, for StablecoinDEX, FeeManager and TIP20ChannelReserve on Tempo, for the B20 factory and Policy Registry on Base, and for BNB Smart Chain after 2026-12-08.

leads.question: Can native value reach the Arc PoolManager without a call to settle or settleFor, for example as the beneficiary of SELFDESTRUCT, as a fee or reward recipient, or through a system transfer, while 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 is the synced currency? Read the SELFDESTRUCT and transfer rules in crates/evm of arc-node and state the answer.
leads.why: balanceOf at 0x3600... is the native balance divided by 10^12 and rounded down (2448892234477 units against 2448892234477765867401833 wei at block 32,753,089). An inflow smaller than 10^12 wei that lifts the remainder over 10^12 between sync and settle is credited as one whole unit (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), which take then pays as 10^12 wei. The gain is below 0.000001 USDC per settle and is paid from the remainder that native payers left, so it is dust, and no other path to it exists because settle rejects value while a token is synced (356). The answer would close the last open detail of the native face item.
